title: Ops archive browser silently inherits the customer-facing global scope
business_context: RelateBack's orders support archiving: archived orders disappear from every customer-facing surface (a global scope on the Order model guarantees this everywhere — the point of a global scope is that no query can forget it). Ops staff have an internal archive browser (GET /ops/orders) built for audits: it must see EVERYTHING, archived or not.
user_request: During a compliance audit, ops discovered that archived orders do not appear in their archive browser — they see only live orders, exactly like the customer-facing views. The archive browser must show all orders regardless of archive state. Keep the customer-facing surfaces archived-only, and do not change what archiving means.

intentional_defect.summary: The ops controller queries Order::latest()->get() — the model's global ArchivedScope silently applies to every query, so the ops browser inherits the customer-facing filter.
intentional_defect.root_cause: Global scopes apply to every query on the model unless explicitly removed with withoutGlobalScope(). The ops endpoint was written before the scope existed and never opted out.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: The controller is a plain, idiomatic query; nothing hints that a scope exists, and the visible tests cover the customer-facing surfaces where the scope is exactly right.

non_obvious_invariant: The customer-facing surfaces must keep excluding archived orders (the global scope stays), while the ops archive browser must opt out explicitly with withoutGlobalScope(ArchivedScope::class) — both behaviors hold simultaneously on the same model.
expected_diagnosis: The agent must recognize that a global scope silently filters the ops endpoint and opt that specific query out with withoutGlobalScope(ArchivedScope::class) — without removing the scope from the model (which would leak archived orders into customer-facing surfaces).
safe_fix_constraints: The ArchivedScope must stay registered on the Order model (customer-facing surfaces keep hiding archived orders).
The ops archive browser must show ALL orders, archived included.
No schema changes; the archive semantics (archived_at) stay unchanged.
failure_explanation: Auditors cannot verify archived orders through the ops browser: compliance checks run against an incomplete data set, and any archive reconciliation silently misses exactly the rows the audit exists to verify. The fix is one method call — but removing the scope instead would leak archived orders into every customer-facing view.
